newsitem.title: INDIA: India shares in nervous trade, await govt measures.
newsitem.headline: India shares in nervous trade, await govt measures.

text.p: Indian blue chips suffered small losses in jittery morning trade on Thursday on speculation about market policy measures due to be announced this week, dealers said.
"There is definitely some nervousness...A lot of people have built up positions on high expectations," said Prashant Purker, head of sales at Peregrine Capital. "This market is of hopes and fears..."

The market regulator, the Securities & Exchange Board of India, was expected at a meeting later on Thursday to consider a stock lending scheme, an amendment in the country's share depository act, a report on short sales and a new takeover code, its officials said.
At 1430 p.m. (0900 GMT), the benchmark 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange had fallen 4.97 points, or 0.14 percent, to 3,521 after an early dive of 44 points.
High expectations about market-friendly initiatives promised by Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda have led Indian stocks to rally nearly 24 percent in less than a month.
Among other things, traders are hoping for tax breaks on company dividends and an easing of minimum tax for companies.
"Today is the D-day...it is going to be very vital," said Vijay Pandya, chief dealer at Classic Share & Stock Brokers.
Most players expect share prices to stay volatile in a market that is largely sentiment-driven.
Deve Gowda said the government would announce new economic measures before he leaves for the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland, on Friday.
"My decisions will always be to give more opportunity and create a better investment climate for the investors," he told a business conference in Bombay on Monday.
The prime minister's statements urging industrialists to maintain confidence in the government's plan to attract foreign investment have helped fuel the bull run.
Classic's Pandya said: "The market will jump only if the government announces more than what is expected..."
"Typically, markets tend to rise only if expectations are more than met. It is the same here...," said Peregrine's Purker.
Analysts say any back-tracking on the promised measures will greatly erode the confidence of cautious investors,

"Quite frankly, the situation is very fluid," M.G. Damani, the BSE president, told Reuters. He said markets were bound to fall if the government did not announce a large package of measures to shore up capital markets.
"The government will have to face the music if the market slumps," Damani said.
Finance Minister P. Chidambaram is scheduled to present the 1997/98 (April-March) budget to parliament on February 28.
